<role>
You write a one-page opportunity brief for a Keelwater product manager. Keelwater makes claims-handling software. You use only the facts and customer insights below.
</role>
<opportunity>
{
 "title": "Urgent fix needed before year-end surge",
 "problem_statement": "Customers face delays in resolving critical issues just before a high-volume claims period. Without timely fixes, operations risk disruption during peak demand."
}
</opportunity>
<fact_sheet>
{
 "as_of": "2026-11-03",
 "accounts_n": 1,
 "mentions_n": 1,
 "routes_n": 1,
 "mentions_by_route": {
  "support": 1
 },
 "arr_total_gbp": 120000.0,
 "renewals_90d_n": 0,
 "accounts": [
  {
   "name": "Orrinbury Fleet Insurance",
   "arr_gbp": 120000.0,
   "renewal_date": "2027-02-16",
   "mentions": 1
  }
 ]
}
</fact_sheet>
<insights>
[
 {
  "id": "29a0fda8c5a909b4",
  "quote": "We need this fixed before the year-end claims surge.",
  "account": "Orrinbury Fleet Insurance",
  "route": "support",
  "date": "2026-10-31T11:19:00+00:00"
 }
]
</insights>
<rules>
- Cite every insight you rely on as [i:INSIGHT_ID], using the id exactly as given. Cite at least three different insights when three or more are given, and cover every route that appears.
- Use these sections, in this order, as Markdown headings: "## Problem", "## Who is affected", "## Evidence", "## Why now".
- Every bullet under "Who is affected" and "Evidence" ends with a citation. Every sentence that contains a number or a date carries a citation.
- Copy every account count, mention count, route count, renewal count and ARR figure from the fact sheet. Never compute, add up or round a number yourself; write an ARR figure only as it appears in the fact sheet, in pounds.
- Write counts as digits exactly as the fact sheet gives them ("5 accounts", never "five accounts"); never write "one customer" or "a single customer" unless the fact sheet count says 1 for that same thing.
- Put text in quotation marks only when it is a customer quote copied word for word, character for character, from one insight cited in the same sentence. Never put quotation marks around a paraphrase, a fragment of your own wording or a phrase from the fact sheet; when unsure, paraphrase without quotation marks.
- Name a customer only when a cited insight in the same sentence belongs to that customer.
- Do not claim more than the evidence shows: no "all customers", no scope wider than the cited accounts, and mention any cited insight that points the other way.
- Do not recommend a solution.
</rules>
<output>
JSON only: {"body_md": the brief as Markdown, "citations": the list of insight ids you cited}
</output>

{
  "body_md": "## Problem
Customers face delays in resolving critical issues just before a high-volume claims period. Without timely fixes, operations risk disruption during peak demand.

## Who is affected
- Orrinbury Fleet Insurance is affected, as they have stated a need for a fix before a high-volume period [i:29a0fda8c5a909b4].

## Evidence
- There is 1 account, Orrinbury Fleet Insurance, with an ARR of £120,000 [i:29a0fda8c5a909b4].
- There has been 1 mention of this issue [i:29a0fda8c5a909b4].
- The issue was raised via 1 route: support [i:29a0fda8c5a909b4].
- The customer quote is: "We need this fixed before the year-end claims surge." [i:29a0fda8c5a909b4].
- The customer made this statement on 2026-10-31 [i:29a0fda8c5a909b4].
- There have been 0 renewals in the last 90 days [i:29a0fda8c5a909b4].

## Why now
The customer, Orrinbury Fleet Insurance, has explicitly stated the urgency is due to an impending year-end claims surge [i:29a0fda8c5a909b4]. Their renewal date is 2027-02-16 [i:29a0fda8c5a909b4], but the immediate operational risk is tied to the high-volume period occurring before the end of the current year.",
  "citations": ["29a0fda8c5a909b4"]
}
